Subject: Private offer: commit slope & partner passback mechanics

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. To move this forward we'll need a clear view of how the private offer will appear on our AWS invoice vs what our reseller (CloudBridge) receives.

Two asks from procurement/legal:
- A worked example showing list price, private-offer price, partner passback to CloudBridge (percent and $) at three commit levels (year 1: $250k / $750k / $1.5M).
- Confirmation whether passback is a reduction on Redwood's net invoice to us or a separate payment routed to the partner.

I attached a short summary (BrightEye_Pricing_ASK.pdf) with our target commit bands. Can you route to whoever owns passback mechanics? We need this for our internal SOW and to brief legal.

Target timeline: internal approval by 11/20.

Thanks,
Sarah Johnson

BrightEye Health

- We'll produce a worked example matrix for the three commit levels you listed.
- Typical flow we use is to net the partner passback as a line-item credit on our invoice to you (keeps procurement flow simpler), but we can also support a separate pass-through payment if CloudBridge requires an independent reconciliation.

Ben — can you draft the matrix (breakdown by list price -> private-offer price -> Redwood net -> partner passback absolute/$ and percent) and include an example per-commit band? Use the attached pricing-model.xlsx as the template.

Irene — can you confirm how invoicing looks in the case of a line-item passback vs separate payment and whether there are restrictions for AWS private offers (DocuSign or Marketplace behavior)?

Sarah — we'll aim to have a first draft back by Monday 11/16 so you have time to brief legal.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Hi all — I put together the worked examples and the partner-passback matrix. Summary below and attached as partner-passback-matrix.csv + updated pricing-model.xlsx.

Assumptions (please confirm):
- List price per unit: $0.12/token-equivalent (example metric for the model)
- Private-offer effective discount: we can tier at 10% / 18% / 25% at the three commit bands you requested.
- Partner passback: default 18% of Redwood net for CloudBridge, with floor of $10k in year 1 for the lowest band. We can increase to 22% for the $1.5M commitment band if needed.

Worked example (rounded):
Band A — $250k commit
- List invoice amount: $312,500
- Private-offer price (18% discount off list): $256,250
- Redwood net (after partner passback 18% on net): $210,025
- Partner passback: $46,225

Band B — $750k commit (18% tier)
- List: $937,500
- Private-offer: $768,750
- Redwood net (after 18% passback): $630,375
- Partner passback: $138,375

Band C — $1.5M commit (25% tier, optional 22% partner uplift)
- List: $1,875,000
- Private-offer: $1,406,250
- Redwood net (after 22% passback): $1,097, (see attached for exact)

Notes on mechanics:
- Option 1 (recommended): Redwood invoices BrightEye for the net amount and shows partner passback as a deductible line-item credit (one invoice flow). Pros: single reconciliation for BrightEye, consistent with Marketplace private offer flows.
- Option 2: Redwood issues full private-offer invoice to BrightEye; Redwood issues payment to CloudBridge separately. Pros: cleaner partner accounting for CloudBridge; Cons: doubles reconciliation for BrightEye.

If BrightEye prefers Option 2 due to internal partner controls, we can support it but will need to update the SOW and add a short reconciliation schedule.

I attached the CSV + the populated pricing-model.xlsx. Happy to walk through numbers on a quick screen share.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachments: partner-passback-matrix.csv (worked examples across bands), pricing-model.xlsx (populated)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sarah Johnson <procurement@brighteyehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:20:55 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer: commit slope & partner passback mechanics

Thanks — I reviewed Ben's sheet and pulled the operational constraints. Short answers:

- AWS Private Offer behavior: the Marketplace records the private offer price; any downstream partner passback shown as a credit on Redwood's invoice is reflected in our internal billing system. That is compatible with BrightEye's procurement if you simply treat the invoice net as the payable. No extra fee required from BrightEye.
- Separate partner payments: we can do a separate pass-through payment to CloudBridge (Option 2) but it requires a monthly reconciliation file and a PO amendment to show CloudBridge as beneficiary. That typically adds ~7 business days to first partner payment.
- DocuSign / Marketplace note: DocuSign is only needed for the SOW/terms if BrightEye wants Redwood to explicitly assign the partner passback; otherwise standard private-offer agreement is sufficient.

Operational request from ops side: if BrightEye chooses Option 2, please confirm CloudBridge's payment details and whether they need 1099/contract language. Also confirm whether BrightEye expects passback to be grossed up (i.e., Redwood to show gross and then passback line) or net. The examples Ben provided are net-first.

I added a short ops checklist to the HubSpot deal (link below) for clarity.

Irene Choi
